prompt: Make Java's initialisation order observable: add the static field, static block, instance field, instance initialiser and constructor call so EVENTS records static-field, static-block once, then instance-field, instance-block, constructor per object.
explanation: Class initialisation runs static field initialisers and static blocks once, in the order they are written, the first time the class is used. Object creation then runs instance field initialisers and instance initialiser blocks in textual order, and only afterwards the constructor body. That is why EVENTS has to be declared first -- a static initialiser placed above it would run before the list exists and throw a NullPointerException.
hints: note(...) both records the event and returns the text, so 'private static final String LABEL = note("static-field");' fills the field and logs in one line.
Instance field initialisers and instance initialiser blocks run in the order they appear in the file, before the constructor body.
Keep everything below the EVENTS declaration, and count the object in the constructor with a static int.
